findings.title: Deny-all policy not pinned to executor namespace
findings.problem: The NetworkPolicy is bound to the literal namespace codemie-code-executor; CodeExecutorConfig namespace is configurable and no test ties the manifest to the config default. The compose healthcheck only checks the literal namespace.
findings.impact: A changed default or CODE_EXECUTOR_NAMESPACE runs sandbox pods with no deny-all policy, letting scripts reach postgres and elasticsearch. Reachability of the misconfiguration is unconfirmed (config-dependent).
findings.recommendation: Add a unit test that parses the manifest and asserts the NetworkPolicy and Namespace names equal CodeExecutorConfig.from_env().namespace; optionally fail startup when the configured namespace lacks the policy.

findings.title: Refused counter carries invoked_by=script
findings.problem: send_script_tool_call_metrics adds INVOKED_BY for every kind including REFUSED, while ticket decision 4 lists the refused counter attributes and says no invoked_by; test_outcome_metrics.py asserts the label.
findings.impact: Required spec/story criterion is only partially met: refused-counter series carry a dimension the owner excluded.
findings.recommendation: Omit invoked_by (and base_tool_name/tool_type if not in decision 4) for the REFUSED kind and update the test, or get decision 4 amended.

findings.title: Cancelled code_executor run reported as ok
findings.problem: execute catches only Exception before sandbox_run.fail, while the workspace-script path deliberately catches BaseException so a cancelled run's outcome matches. CancelledError/KeyboardInterrupt leaves outcome ok. The same applies to BatchJobRunner.run.
findings.impact: Cancelled runs inflate the success counters of the sandbox run metrics; the two sandbox tools disagree. Reachability of cancellation here was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Use except BaseException as error: sandbox_run.fail(error); raise in CodeExecutorTool.execute and BatchJobRunner.run.
